submitter: bugs_open/408 fix (routed via the bugfix_357 lane's HANDOFF_2026-08-26b, 'What to do, in order' item 1). Single coherent task: make extractFieldValue's non-termination unrepresentable.
rationale: extractFieldValue (multipage_actions.go:1186 pre-change) had two fallbacks for an unresolvable dotted path that are exact inverses: one strips '.response.' and recurses, the other inserts it and recurses. Each call satisfies the other's condition, so any content_field that resolves on no form recursed until the goroutine stack passed 1 GB and the runtime killed the pod - measured 2026-08-26: exitCode 2, a container log that is one repeated Warn line 12,654 times out of 12,654, three orchestrations abandoned at build_pages_loop_iter_0_assemble_page and released only by the 4h stale reaper. The trigger is a NORMAL outcome (a page the content writer skips) and also any operator typo in content_field, since that is step config. The fix is the bug file's candidate 1, the shape three sibling resolvers in this package already use (getNestedFieldValue in hitl_request_human_input.go:684, resolveFieldPathForSpawn in spawn_actions.go:3221, resolveFieldPathCallAgent in call_agent.go:173): resolve against a bounded ordered candidate list in a loop, via a plain iterative walk helper, with no self-call anywhere - non-termination becomes structurally impossible rather than merely guarded. The candidate list is generated to be EXACTLY the sequence of forms the old recursion tried before it began to cycle (original; each '.response.' stripped in turn; the fully-stripped form with '.response.' re-inserted after the first segment, skipped when identical to the original), so every path that terminated correctly before resolves to the same value via the same form, and the only behaviour change is non-termination -> empty string. A naive flat three-candidate list would have narrowed resolution on multi-occurrence and non-first-segment '.response.' shapes (a.b.response.c also tries a.response.b.c today and terminates if it resolves); the loop builder preserves those routes, and two table rows pin them. The sole caller (1 caller as of 2026-09-02, AssemblePageAction :106) already treats empty string as 'skip this page', so no call site changes. The per-recursion Warn is demoted: one Warn per failed lookup, message and keys preserved ('Field not found in path', field/full_path) with an additive paths_tried key, per-candidate attempts at Debug. The walk distinguishes key-missing (try next candidate) from non-map-mid-path (return empty outright), preserving the old default-branch short-circuit, and drops one provably dead branch (ExtractStepData applied to a value already known absent: its argument is nil, and ExtractStepData returns a non-map argument as-is, data_helpers.go 'Not a map, return as-is', so the branch could never fire). SCOPE: unexported function, one caller, no new config key (RFC_022 budget untouched), no shared-mechanism guarantee changed - by the 2026-07-29 ruling this is a normal council-gate change, not architecture-scope. Deliberately NOT done here: unifying the ~14 near-clone dot-path walkers (LANDMINES.md dotted-path-resolver entry) - the siblings' candidate orders genuinely differ (hitl tries add-then-strip; spawn/call_agent add-only; multipage strip-chain-then-add), so consolidation changes resolution semantics for somebody and belongs to its own track.

plan.summary: Replace extractFieldValue's two mutually-recursive .response. fallbacks with a bounded ordered-candidate loop over a new plain iterative walk helper (walkFieldPath), preserving every terminating resolution route, converting the non-terminating case to the caller's documented empty-string contract, and collapsing the 12,654-line Warn flood to one Warn per failed lookup. Plus a table-driven termination test run under go test -timeout whose crash-input rows are the behavioural guard, proven able to fail by running the exact crash input against the old function verbatim (FAIL by stack overflow in 3.7s).

edits.rationale: The single walk, extracted so the candidate loop cannot re-grow a self-call - the family convention (traverseNestedPath, traverseFieldPath, traverseFieldPathGeneric all sit under their candidate-ordering wrappers). Log-free and pure; returns the failing segment so the caller logs once. The three-valued outcome is load-bearing: key-missing admits another candidate, non-map-mid-path must end the lookup outright or the old semantics widen.

plan.risks: 1. CANDIDATE ORDER IS MULTIPAGE'S OWN, NOT THE FAMILY'S: hitl tries add before strip; spawn/call_agent try add only. Unifying orders changes which value wins on inputs where two forms both resolve, so it is refused here and named as the separate consolidation track (concept-register entry first, consolidation only as its own RFC if ever needed). 2. LOG CONSUMERS: 'Field not found in path' and 'Cannot traverse further, value is not a map' keep message and field/full_path keys verbatim; paths_tried is additive; volume drops from one-per-recursion to one-per-lookup, which is the fix; a lookup that succeeds via a fallback now logs no Warn at all (previously one per failed hop) - intended. 3. THE DEAD-BRANCH REMOVAL IS SEVERABLE: if a reviewer reads the ExtractStepData branch as live, it can be restored verbatim without weakening the termination property. 4. INERT UNTIL ROLLED: platform Go - the bug stays open until an image at or after the fix commit is built (bumped IMAGE_TAG, never same-tag) and verified at the pod via the build-provenance stamp with git merge-base --is-ancestor, per service. 5. VERIFICATION VACUITY, named in advance: after the roll, a green rebuild of the crashing page proves ONLY pod survival and a terminal orchestration (the whole chain SKIPS: git_commit via checkUpstreamSkipped, save_sections at len(sections)==0) - it is NOT evidence for the 357 lane's precondition 4, per that lane's Finding 1 and bugs_open/408 section 8.
